artist.title: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artist.description: Children's games, proverbs, a wedding feast and a fall nobody notices: Bruegel filled every canvas with small stories. Follow them one detail at a time.
artist.attributionNote: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus is attributed to Bruegel: lab tests suggest the canvas dates from after his death, so it may be a copy of a lost original.

about.intro: On Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube, @zoomed.art takes one painting and looks closer, detail by detail. Here, there is room to stay with the canvas beyond a 59-second reel.

sections.title: The camera moves. The painting never changes.
sections.text: The artworks are historical documents. We move the view, frame a detail and give the story space. We do not redraw, recolour or animate the painting's figures.

sections.title: A story you can check.
sections.text: Our editorial standard is to check facts against sources and label interpretations as interpretations. Each painting page has space for its sources and image credit.

sections.title: A closer look, in your hands.
sections.text: Follow the guided story, explore the canvas freely, or read the full article. The painting is always the centre of the experience.

editorialPolicy.title: Look closely. Check the story.
editorialPolicy.description: How Zoomed Art treats facts, interpretations and the paintings themselves.
editorialPolicy.intro: A painting deserves care, and so does the story told about it. These are the standards behind Zoomed Art.

sections.title: Facts and sources
sections.text: We check factual claims against sources before a story is published. The source list belongs with the article so readers can follow the evidence.

sections.title: Interpretation is labelled
sections.text: An interpretation is not presented as a verified fact. Language such as “many see” or “tradition says” makes that distinction visible.

sections.title: The artwork stays intact
sections.text: We use public-domain paintings from Wikimedia Commons and museum open collections. Camera movement and focus frames guide the eye; the artwork is not redrawn, recoloured, AI-animated or altered into a new composition.

sections.title: Image credits
sections.text: Each painting page names the museum that holds the work and links to the public-domain image on Wikimedia Commons where the exact file is recorded.

sections.title: What is still being prepared
sections.text: Every painting already has its guided story, written from checked facts. Long-form articles, artist biographies and full source lists are added one painting at a time; until a painting has them, its page is not offered to search engines.

sections.title: Corrections
sections.text: If you find an error, message @zoomed.art on Instagram with the painting title, the passage or detail, and a source we can check.
